subject: Biology
title: The Brain Stem: Life Support
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Brain Stem: Life Support usable.

hook.text: The brain stem sits at the base of your brain and keeps you alive without you ever thinking about it.

buildup.text: It controls breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, and swallowing—automatic survival functions.

discovery.text: All sensory and motor signals between brain and body pass through the brain stem.

twist.text: The brain stem is evolutionary ancient. Reptiles have one too—it's the 'lizard brain.'

climax.text: Brain stem death means the body can't sustain itself, even if the cortex is still intact.

punchline.text: The oldest part of your brain keeps you breathing.

quiz.question: What vital functions does the brain stem control?
options: Breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure

details.summary: The brain stem controls essential life functions including breathing, heart rate, blood pressure, swallowing, and consciousness. It connects the brain to the spinal cord and manages automatic processes that sustain life without conscious effort.
details.whyItMatters: Brain stem damage is often fatal because it controls functions essential for survival. Brain death is legally defined as irreversible loss of brain stem function, making it the most critical brain structure for sustaining life.
takeaways: The brain stem controls breathing, heart rate, and blood pressure
It contains the reticular formation that regulates consciousness and arousal
Brain stem death is the legal definition of death in many countries

faq.question: What are the three parts of the brain stem?
faq.answer: The midbrain processes visual and auditory reflexes. The pons relays signals between the cerebrum and cerebellum and helps regulate breathing. The medulla oblongata controls heart rate, blood pressure, and breathing, the most essential survival functions.

faq.question: Why is brain stem damage so dangerous?
faq.answer: The brain stem controls involuntary life-sustaining functions. Damage can stop breathing, collapse blood pressure, or eliminate consciousness. Even small lesions in the brain stem can be fatal because the critical structures are densely packed.
